regions.name: flow_near_wake
regions.why: Create the missing off-body near-wake box so the separated-shear-layer / bluff-body wake envelope is covered. Bounds are the flow_requirement:near_wake envelope padded by ~0.01 m so the float32 bounds (0.3499999940/1.0499999821/+-0.9799999833/+-0.4899999917) are strictly contained. Level 2 gives 0.04375 m, half the 0.0875 m prior (= exactly level 1), leaving a factor-2 margin for the native p95 span statistic (tolerance 1.5) instead of a knife-edge equality. Level 2 stays coarser than surface level 3, so no surface/layer/quality setting changes and the surface -> wake -> background grading is preserved. Volume 0.72*1.98*1.00 = 1.43 m^3, ~1.7e4 cells. This is an envelope prior, not a measured shear-layer thickness.

regions.name: flow_far_wake
regions.why: Cover the downstream velocity-deficit/shear transport envelope, padded ~0.01-0.02 m beyond the float32 bounds (1.0499999821/2.4499999583/+-1.2599999785/+-0.6299999893). The prior span 0.175 m is EXACTLY the uniform background cell (grading 1.0), so leaving it unboxed relies on an equality that any stricter native comparison or transition cell would break; level 1 = 0.0875 m supplies a factor-2 margin at ~6.9e3 cells. The upstream face overlaps the near-wake box by 0.02 m so maximum level wins and no coarse slot appears between the two envelopes. Kept deliberately at one increment (the scenario states coarser far-wake bounds cost), not refined to surface level.

regions.name: repair_0
regions.why: actual layer deficit concentrated in measured boundary faces

advisor.hypothesis: The layer failure is NOT a missing-cell / resolution problem: global surface level 3 gives 0.021875 m surface cells, and the mid-body curved lateral surface (|Y|<0.5, where coverage_5plus = 1.00, all area at 8 layers) already extrudes perfectly. The loss is concentrated at the two streamwise end rims (Y = +-0.70): the layer_shortfall:0 cluster spans y = 0.5859..0.7437, x/z = +-0.393 with 810 wall points at ~2.35e-6 m wall distance, and the dihedral statistics there (p50 45 deg, p95 90 deg, 50% of adjacent edges above the 60 deg layer feature_angle) show a sharp cylinder/end-cap crease. The y-band [0.55,0.8] reaches only 0.449 coverage-5plus with 12.7% of area stuck at 1 layer; the crease splits a maximally thin requested stack (0.00107 m first layer, 0.01766 m, only 1.6% of the 0.35 m cap radius). So layer feature_angle 60 deg suppresses extrusion across the 90 deg rim, and the medial-axis mover dissipates local normal/proximity information there (the "Inserting points ... if angle to nearest layer patch > 30 degrees" logic and medial smoothing). This is a corner/shrinking defect, not underresolution. Fix: reduce the first-layer step (finer absolute first height) with a smaller expansion ratio so the dimensionless step is more forgiving, widen the layer angle so the crease extrudes, enlarge the medial corridor allowance, and increase normal + thickness smoothing so the rim displacement is redistributed instead of collapsing. The transition/concave clusters (concaveCells:10, 1141 cells, y up to 0.929) sit outside the body footprint but overlap the near-wake envelope; they are a transition-quality artifact of the surface -> wake -> background grading and are addressed by safer snap normal smoothing, not by coarser layers.
advisor.expected_change: In-region coverage_5plus for the end-rim band [y 0.55..0.80] should rise from 0.449 toward >>0.90, and whole-body layer coverage from 0.797 above the 0.90 gate, with 8 actual layers retained on the lateral surface and no new nonpositive cells (must stay above min_vol 1e-13, max_non_ortho gate 65, max_boundary_skewness 20, min_face_weight 0.02). Stack thickness drops from 0.01766 m to ~0.0110 m (a 38% reduction, still ~2% of the 0.35 m cap radius), so wall-distance step is finer and the crease has more room. Uncertainty: the self-intersection reason is reported as "failed/unavailable", i.e. no native positive evidence exists, so I cannot assert the crease diagnosis is the only cause; the concaveCells:10 transition cluster at 0.074 m wall distance may persist or shift. No flow solution exists, so y+ is not claimed - the finer first height only biases estimated y+ downward from the flat-plate p50 50.

actions.why: Treat the crease as a layer-step/corner-extrusion defect. Halve the absolute first height to 5.35e-4 m and drop the expansion ratio to 1.08 so the per-layer step at the 45-90 deg rim is much gentler; reduce n_surface_layers 8 -> 7 to keep the total stack at ~0.0110 m (vs the 0.01528 m estimated boundary layer), well under the ~0.12 m (0.35 m cap-radius budget under max_thickness_to_medial_ratio 0.45). Raise feature_angle 60 -> 90 so the rim can participate in extrusion, keep min_medial_axis_angle at 90 (medialAxisMeshMover tests thickness/medialDist times the extrusion-to-medial dot product; the rim is the near-perpendicular case where the mover hoists thickness), raise max_thickness_to_medial_ratio 0.3 -> 0.45 for corridor headroom, and strengthen n_smooth_normals 3 -> 12 and n_smooth_thickness 10 -> 20 so displacement is redistributed over the rim instead of collapsing to 1-4 layers. n_grow stays 0 because it propagates NON-EXTRUSION and would lower coverage further. mesh_shrinker stays displacementMedialAxis (the torus ablation shows a shrinker swap alone is not a general repair).

The concaveCells:10 transition cluster (1141 cells at 0.074 m wall distance, spanning the near-wake envelope) and the small concaveFaces clusters point at snapped transition faces rather than layers. Increase feature-snap iterations and relax iterations and switch on implicit feature snap so the rim and cap edges are captured on the surface before extrusion; a cleaner edge helps the layer pass extrude at the crease. Keep tolerance 2.0 and raise patch smoothing to smooth transition faces without shrinking the surface.

Add one isotropic increment around the end-rim band where the shortfall clusters sit (y 0.55..0.80 and the mirrored -0.80..-0.55), using the measured cluster bounds +-0.393 in x/z padded to +-0.42. Level 4 = 0.010938 m halves the local wall face size so the extruded column has more support at the crease, and stays within global surface level 3 + 1. Cost is small because the band is ~0.03 m^3 x 2.

Mirror the rim refinement on the other end cap (y -0.80..-0.55) so both 45-90 deg creases are treated symmetrically; layer_shortfall:0 and :1 are mirrored pairs (centroids at y = +-0.6825, count 810 each).

alternatives: Only widen feature_angle 60 -> 90 and keep the original 8 layers at 0.00107 m first height: safest cost-wise, but leaves the crease with the same dimensionless first-layer step, which the measured 12.7%-at-1-layer fraction suggests is marginal.
Only refine the rims to level 4 (no layer change): adds support around the crease but does not fix a suppression/step mechanism, and the mid-body is already at 8 layers.

Switch mash_shrinker to displacementMotionSolver: rejected as primary because the torus ablation left only 1.74% adequate coverage from a shrinker swap alone; kept as a fallback only if the medial mover still truncates.
Raise n_grow to 2: rejected, since nGrow spreads NON-EXTRUSION and lowers coverage, the opposite of the failing direction.
counterevidence: The mid-body lateral surface (|Y|<0.5) already has coverage_5plus = 1.00 with 100% of area at 8 layers, so neither the surface level 3 nor the general layer stack is globally broken; only the rim band is deficient (0.449).

native_thickness_truncation retained 0 truncation lines and 'Reducing layer thickness at 0 nodes', so explicit medial-distance truncation is NOT the recorded mechanism; my mechanism must be corner suppression at the 45-90 deg crease plus a marginal layer step, not medial truncation.

The failure reason says self-intersection evidence 'failed/unavailable', so no native positive self-intersection record exists; I cannot assert the inverted-mesh story from measurement, only from the 90 deg dihedral p95 and the >60 deg layer-angle edge fraction of 0.5.

The concaveCells:10 cluster spans y -0.927..+0.929, i.e. wider than the body, and sits at 0.074 m wall distance, which is outside the extruded stack (0.0177 m) - so it is more likely a snapped transition-face artifact than a layer artifact, which is why I also make a snap change rather than assuming all of it is layers.
No flow solution exists (flow_probe_sanity null), so no y+ improvement can be claimed and wall_height is not used.
